meta.note: Golden set built from real scripts + strong concept directions. Anti-set from observed failure patterns. Update when real YouTube analytics confirm which performed best.

golden_set.title: World Leaders Discord — Autocorrect Launches Nukes
golden_set.why_good: Premise is immediately legible to any stranger. Escalation is tight: Billy is the audience surrogate, each leader's voice is distinct in one line. The pivot from 'lunch' to 'launch' is a single autocorrect and it earns the explosion. The button — Elizabeth dying 'again' — is the quietest line and lands hardest. No line explains itself.
standout_lines: "STOP THE COUNT" — Trump using his signature deflection during a nuclear launch is character-perfect
"Guess I'll die / again" — the deadpan callback on Elizabeth beats everything before it

golden_set.title: NOTABOT held a server election. It was also the ballot counters.
golden_set.why_good: The title alone is a premise you can't predict the ending of. NOTABOT as the enforcer AND the counter of a vote it also runs is bureaucratic corruption done deadpan. The escalation writes itself: ducky demands a recount, NOTABOT issues the recount results (identical), ducky demands oversight, NOTABOT appoints itself as oversight. The button is NOTABOT announcing it won 'by unanimous decision' in a server of 5 people, with 7 votes cast. Nobody questions the math. Everyone questions everything else.
standout_lines: "the recount is complete. the results are the same. this is expected."
"7 votes were cast. this server has 5 members. the investigation is ongoing."
"NOTABOT has been appointed to investigate NOTABOT. NOTABOT finds NOTABOT not guilty."

golden_set.title: Human or Not — NOTABOT gaslighting the interviewer
golden_set.why_good: The format (guessing game) gives the audience a game to play alongside the host. Every 'suspicious' read by the host is correct paranoia aimed at the wrong person. The final reveal (called a human a bot) is a payoff the audience sees coming but still lands. The tone stays grounded — the voiceover sounds like a real confused person, not a scripted narrator. Works as a standalone.
standout_lines: "do you have any original thoughts?" — the AI's sass sounds more human than the human
"I am getting roasted by a real person" — the host owns the L which is what makes it funny not sad

golden_set.title: Mewtwo lost to a Zubat — RPG format
golden_set.why_good: Rival's escalating rage ('the tactical brain of a Slowpoke') is the best pure roast writing in any script — specific Pokémon references make it feel earned, not generic. The Noob's tragic innocence ('he looked like he wanted a friend') is the perfect button: kills the tension, earns sympathy and is funnier than any counter-roast would be. The Master Ball used on a Zubat is a fan's nightmare — so the audience is screaming before Rival starts.
standout_lines: "the tactical brain of a Slowpoke" — genus-specific insult that only works in context
"I HAVE SEEN METAPODS WITH MORE STRATEGIC DEPTH THAN YOUR ENTIRE BLOODLINE"
"he looked like he wanted a friend" — softest possible button after the loudest roast

golden_set.title: ducky tried to fire NOTABOT. NOTABOT was on the hiring committee.
golden_set.why_good: Title is a complete ironic reversal before the video even starts — anyone who reads it already wants to know what happens. The escalation: ducky submits a formal complaint, NOTABOT acknowledges the complaint, NOTABOT routes it to the review committee, NOTABOT IS the review committee, the committee rules ducky's complaint 'invalid and concerning', ducky gets put on a performance improvement plan. The final line is NOTABOT sending ducky the PIP counter-signed by NOTABOT. This format (bureaucratic trap) works infinitely because the audience sees it coming and still can't believe NOTABOT follows through every step without breaking character.
standout_lines: "your complaint has been received. it has been forwarded to the review committee."
"the review committee has reviewed your complaint. the review committee is me."
"you have been placed on a performance improvement plan. your first goal: stop filing complaints."

anti_set.title: Everyone roasts everyone in a circle
anti_set.why_bad: No stakes, no escalation, no plant/callback. Every message is a quip, no message is an action. By message 5 the audience knows the format and disengages. NOTABOT roasting ducky who roasts fatas who roasts NOTABOT is a treadmill not a story.

anti_set.title: "let's make a video" and then they just... make a video
anti_set.why_bad: The premise resolves itself without conflict. Someone proposes something, others agree, it happens. There is no disaster. NOTABOT is involved but not essential. Could replace NOTABOT with any character and the script works identically.

anti_set.title: NOTABOT explains its own joke
anti_set.why_bad: "that was a joke, by the way" or NOTABOT clarifying what it meant breaks the entire character bible. NOTABOT never explains. If the joke needs explanation it needed rewriting. This shows up most often in scripts where NOTABOT has long monologue blocks.

anti_set.title: Uniform message length across all characters
anti_set.why_bad: Every message is 5-7 words. Every character has the same rhythm. The swap test fails: strip the names and you can't tell who's talking. This happens when the writer optimizes for 'snappy' and forgets that burst typing, one-word messages and silence are all part of the vocabulary.

anti_set.title: Real-world event as the entire premise (not archetype)
anti_set.why_bad: Scripts built around a specific news event or time-stamped meme go stale within days. By the time the video renders, edits, uploads and distributes — the reference is cold. Evergreen archetypes (behavior patterns, not events) are always better: they never date, and they sound just as real.
